beliefs: f splits the input on whitespace runs, reverses each segment, and joins the reversed segments with single spaces [E1, E2, E3, E4]
Case is preserved; only character order within each whitespace-delimited segment is reversed [E1]
Punctuation adjacent to a word is part of that segment and is reversed with it, e.g. 'a,b'->'bb,a' and 'hello world!'->'olleh !!dlrow' [E2]
Whitespace runs (including leading/trailing and repeated spaces/tabs/newlines) act as separators; leading/trailing whitespace is dropped and internal runs become a single space [E3, E4]
The join uses a single space between reversed segments, but the observed 'x  y  z'->'x y zz' suggests the last segment may absorb an extra character; unclear? [E4]
notes: E4 confirms whitespace collapsing and per-segment reversal, but 'x  y  z'->'x y zz' has an extra 'z' not explained by simple join; I keep the simple rule and flag the anomaly as uncertain.
